core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case (proof lines 8305-8320): the assertion is local on Y and on Y', so the author assumes everything affine, where finiteness makes the rings finite over the base rings.

Compare both sides (proof lines 8320-8340): in the affine case the pushforwards are computed by the sections over the base changes, and the two sides give the same ring-theoretic description, which is the equality asserted.
Conclude (proof lines 8340-8347): the local computation descends to the general case.
proof_roadmap: Localise and use finiteness to reduce to the affine case.
Compute both pushforwards through their sections over the base changes.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves base change for the pushforward along a finite morphism: f'_*(g')^{-1}F = g^{-1}f_*F for any sheaf of sets on X_etale (statement lines 8291-8303). The proof reduces to the affine case by locality and finiteness (proof lines 8305-8320), computes both sides through their sections over the base change (proof lines 8320-8340), and descends the local equality (proof lines 8340-8347). The non-formal content is the affine computation; the argument parallels the integral case with finiteness replacing integrality. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one affine computation.
